_comment: Curated root causes for scripts/app-suite --app writebook. Unpassed tests are
clustered mechanically by failure message; this file is what turns a cluster
into a named todo with an owner. Rules are tried in order; FIRST MATCH WINS,
so the specific ones sit above the general ones.
`match` keys on the failure MESSAGE. A rule may add `match_test`, keyed on
the test identifier, and then both have to hold — which is the only way to
name a SILENT divergence, since every wrong answer reads as the same
assertion failure.
The unit is an UNPASSED TEST, not a FAIL line: a file that dies at load
contributes its whole count against its load error. See the header of
scripts/app-suite-summary.
Empty on purpose: Writebook is the second app suite, and none of its
failures has been triaged into a rule yet. The untriaged cluster on the
page is the todo — add a rule here once a root cause is known.
owner:
compiler — roundhouse modeling debt. Ours to fix.
app      — a Writebook idiom that could change upstream. Only ever a
plain-Rails change that stands on its own merits under stock
Rails; the port never asks for app-side divergence.
gem      — a gem whose surface we shim, or one deliberately out of scope.
spinel   — upstream spinel.
harness  — this harness's own gap, not the emit's.
subset   — the test reaches for dynamic Ruby no compiled target has
(a per-object `extend`, `define_method`, `eval`). Nobody
can act: not a todo, named so it is not triaged twice, and
left out of the who-can-act line.
unknown  — the cluster is real, its root cause is not yet known.
